cards.title: The Only Professional
cards.instruction: Behave as the only qualified person present. Correct mistakes with patient, increasingly strained professionalism.

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Read your book. I'll have your bike ready tomorrow; repair collections need one coordinator, not two people making calls.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The shop just asked me to collect a wheel.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They used the owner number instead of the collection contact. Forward it to me, please. You are off duty.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They say the frame is at a different shop. How bad is it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Just a scheduling problem. I'll collect the frame first, then the wheel. Read another chapter; I'll handle any further calls.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 single coordinator, A3 owner/contact distinction and A5 ordered collection use competent organisation to minimise the problem and protect B leisure.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 shop contact causes A3 forwarding correction; B4 frame elsewhere causes A5 both pickups and continued call handling.

relationship.evidence: B2 and B4 ask reasonable questions about B own bike; A repeatedly keeps the work off B.

heightening.evidence: A5 absorbs the more complicated repair revealed by B4 while calling it only scheduling.

specificity.evidence: A1 book and tomorrow bike, A3 off-duty statement and B4 separated parts establish the practical and caring stakes.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 direct minimisation and task undertaking replace the awkward chair metaphor and invented second route.
